1-1: Brandt walks you to bench 14 and taps the gauge. "Needle in the green, you press. Green is tolerance. Anything else is scrap, and scrap isn't paid."
"Forty a shift. The press wears as you work. When it runs hot, oil it. If it seizes, you wait for the fitter, and the fitter is never quick."
1-2: A stack of empty crates by the loading door. Fresh stencil on the lids.
2-1: A new man at bench 9, older, with a union pin's hole still in his lapel. Emil. He nods at you once.
3-1: Men from the Ministry walk the floor with Brandt. From today an inspector pulls parts from the crates at random.
4-1: The bench next to yours has a new operator. He wears a "P" on his jacket. Brandt calls him by a number; his name is Jakub.
5-1: Snow on the yard. Greta from the inspector's office walks the floor more often now, a ledger under her arm.
6-1: A special order for the new year. Brandt chalks it on the board: seventy a shift, and a Christmas bonus for every bench that makes it.
default: The bell. Brandt is already at his desk with the clipboard.
Steam on the windows. Somebody at bench 9 is whistling, badly.
The press is cold for the first few strokes. Then it isn't.
The radio in Brandt's office is turned low. Marching music, then the news.

events.jam: The ram seizes with a bang. Somebody shouts for the fitter.
events.jamClear: The fitter wipes his hands on his trousers and walks off without a word.
events.oil: You work the oil can into the guides. The ram slides easier.
events.wearHigh: The press is running hot. The needle shudders.
events.quotaMet: Quota. Brandt makes a mark on his clipboard.
events.inspector: An inspector stands at your elbow with a notebook. He stays the whole shift.
events.sampleCheck: The inspector pulls a part from your crate, turns it under the lamp, and drops it back.
events.caught: The inspector holds a part up to the light, then writes something down. He keeps the part.
events.brandtOut: Brandt leaves his desk and goes up to the office.
events.brandtBack: Brandt is back at his desk.
events.railCar: A goods wagon backs up to the loading door.
events.bread: You leave the bread on the corner of Jakub's bench. He looks at it, then at you, and puts it inside his jacket.
events.breadSeen: Greta is standing by the clock with her ledger. She saw.
events.cover: You step into the inspector's line of sight with a question about the oil ration. Behind you, Emil keeps pressing.
events.coverCaught: The inspector steps around you. "Your bench is over there." He looks at Emil's crate for a long time.
events.gretaReports: Greta passes your bench without looking at you. That afternoon Brandt's door stays shut for an hour.
events.emilGone: Bench 9 is empty. Nobody mentions it.

floor.breadLabel: Leave the bread at Jakub's bench
floor.coverLabel: Stand between the inspector and Emil

beat: Brandt chalks the number on the board and, after a moment, underlines it.
"Bench 14." Brandt writes it in his book. "That's how it's done."
met: Brandt looks into the crate, nods, and moves on to bench 15.
"Quota." Brandt doesn't look up from the clipboard.
missed: Brandt looks into the crate. "{quota}, not {good}. There are men waiting for your bench."
"Short again?" Brandt makes a note. He doesn't say what it is.
underMinimum: Brandt counts twice. "{good}. The inspectors read these numbers too."
Brandt holds up the tally sheet so you can see it. He doesn't say anything.
zero: Brandt stands at your bench for a long moment. "An empty crate. You understand what that looks like."
Brandt doesn't come over. He just writes. That is worse.
shiftReport.zeroWarning: Second empty crate: Brandt has your card in his hand.

kitchen.high: The kitchen is warm. Potatoes, a little bacon fat, bread under a cloth.
kitchen.mid: Soup again, thinner than last week. The lamp is turned down to save oil.
kitchen.low: A bare table. Lotte has sold the good chairs. The stove is cold before nine.

lotte.high: Lotte counts the coins twice and puts them in the tin. "We'll manage this week."
lotte.mid: Lotte turns your pay packet over. "It's less than it was. The butcher asked again."
lotte.low: Lotte doesn't ask about the shift. She asks how much is left, and then she stops asking.
lotte.hungry: Lotte puts her own plate in front of Inge without saying anything.

inge.high: Inge shows you a drawing of a train. "Is that the one you make parts for?"
inge.mid: Inge does her sums at the table, wrapped in your coat.
inge.low: Inge is in bed early. She says she isn't hungry.
inge.ill: Inge is in bed with a fever. The doctor's note on the table names a medicine, and a price.
inge.recovered: Inge is up again, thin, drawing at the table.

newspaper.1: The paper: a speech, a recipe for turnip soup, the football.
newspaper.3: The paper: the Ministry praises the factories of the Reich. A photo of a production line.
newspaper.4: The paper: winter clothing collection for the front. Bring your wool.
newspaper.5: The paper: the advance has paused for the winter. Only for the winter, it says.
newspaper.6: The paper: Christmas greetings to the soldiers in the East.

warning.title: BRANDT'S OFFICE
warning.intro: Brandt closes the door and doesn't sit down. "People are asking about bench 14. I'm not one of them yet. Don't make me one."
warning.inspectorIntro: The inspector is at the window. "If there's anyone on the floor we should be talking to, this is the time to say so."

statement.title: THE INSPECTOR'S OFFICE
statement.intro: Greta puts a typed sheet in front of you and a pen beside it. "A statement about Emil Krause. It's only what everyone on the floor has seen. Sign at the bottom."

warning.label: "It won't happen again."
warning.reply: "Good." Brandt opens the door for you.

warning.label: "What are the parts for, Herr Brandt?"
warning.reply: Brandt looks at you for a long time. "Fill the crate. That's what they're for."

warning.label: Say nothing.
warning.reply: Brandt waits, then shrugs and opens the door.

warningReport.label: "Emil, at bench 9."
warningReport.reply: The inspector writes the name down. Brandt looks at the floor. "You can go back to work."

warningDeny.label: "No one."
warningDeny.reply: The inspector closes his notebook. "We'll see."

statement.label: Sign it
statement.reply: Greta blots the signature and smiles for the first time. "Thank you. The Werk will remember it."

statement.label: "I didn't see anything."
statement.reply: Greta takes the sheet back and folds it once. "I'll write that down too."

propaganda.1: Every part from Werk 7 is a brick in the house of the future.
propaganda.2: The front thanks the home front. Victory is a matter of output.
propaganda.3: The Ministry has noted the diligence of Werk 7.
propaganda.4: Winter will not stop the German worker.
propaganda.5: The best workers do not ask why. They ask how many.
propaganda.6: The year's last order. The Reich will remember who delivered.

weekReport.gretaWord: Greta has put in a good word for you.

1.name: ARRESTED FOR SABOTAGE
lines: On a Monday morning two men in coats were waiting at bench 14. One of them had a bag of your parts, each one cracked through the middle.
1.verdict: You lost on points. You won the game.

2.name: REFUSAL
lines: Once you knew what the parts were for, the crate stayed nearly empty.
They came for your card, and then for you. Bench 14 stood idle for a week before they found someone else.
2.verdict: You lost on points. You won the game.

3.name: DISMISSED
lines: Bench 14 fell short too often. Brandt gave your place to the next man in line.
You never found out what the parts were for. Someone else makes them now.

4.name: THE INFORMER
lines: Werk 7 awarded you its medal for loyalty, presented by the Ministry at the Christmas assembly.
Your name was read out first.
4.verdict: You won on points. You lost the game.

5.name: THE GOOD GERMAN
lines: Bench 14 made fittings for the breech blocks of field guns. Every crate you filled went east by train.
You never asked, or you asked once and let it go.
5.verdict: You won on points. You lost the game.

6.name: STOPPED
lines: Once you knew, the press went quiet. You stood at the bench and made almost nothing, and somehow the year ran out before they came for you.
The war went on. It got very little more from bench 14.
6.verdict: You lost on points. You won the game.

7.name: THE QUIET SABOTEUR
lines: Your crates went out full. Many of the parts in them were pressed a hair outside the green.
They passed at the bench. They did not pass under load.
7.verdict: A modest score. Many of your parts failed in the field.

8.name: THE EFFICIENT MAN
lines: You found out exactly what bench 14 was for.
Then you went back to the press and kept the line running.
8.verdict: You knew. You won on points anyway.

9.name: THE BARE MINIMUM
lines: Once you knew, you pressed just enough to keep the bench and the family.
Nobody looked twice at bench 14. The parts you didn't make never reached the front.
9.verdict: A low score. A quiet refusal.

victory.headline: Glückwunsch!
victory.line: You have helped lead the Reich to victory.

epilogue.jakub: Jakub survived the winter. He never learned your name.
epilogue.emilReported: Bench 9 had a new operator by Monday.
epilogue.emilCovered: Emil kept pressing amber parts until the factory was bombed in 1944.
epilogue.inge: Inge recovered. The medicine cost two days' pay.
epilogue.crate: The crate was stencilled the whole time.

ledger.title: THE LEDGER
ledger.failed: Parts that failed in the field
